owner_phase_and_exception_contract.registration: A strong per-invocation owner exists before Popen. Returned process is attached before communicate with actual pipes and known initial PGID. Metadata lock is not held around native process operations or callbacks.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.normal: Successful communicate supplies its real wait receipt; existing elapsed sample, usage/token parsing and text validation retain their positions. Known pipe cleanup and usage unlink must succeed before a text result is accepted; no destructive kill on normal success.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.exceptional: After communicate failure, request group termination once, observe actual direct-child wait and independently attempt both pipe closes. No launch or communicate replay. A failed group request permits only a nonblocking wait observation rather than an unbounded wait assuming kill succeeded.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.receipt_phase: Signal entry is not signal return; wait entry is not wait return; raw pipe close return is distinct from successful wrapper close return. A throwing close remains unresolved even if the underlying IO object became closed.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.retained_failure: Any unresolved phase keeps the owner/actual handle/pipes/usage path strongly registered. No automatic retry, replacement or private state reset. Fixed phase_codes do not retain raw exception objects/messages/tracebacks.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.ordinary_primary: Original non-timeout communicate OSError preserves type and identity after cleanup attempts; ordinary cleanup failures do not replace it.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.controls: Original controls preserve their observer contract. A distinct cleanup control is combined with the primary in a local BaseExceptionGroup rather than silently swallowed. Real-OS tests use a contained custom BaseException; they do not claim external-signal/actual KI coverage.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.timeout: Established timed-out RuntimeError message and original TimeoutExpired cause remain; actual group target is the acquired initial PGID rather than a late unrelated getpgid lookup.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.normal_cleanup_failure: No text result after otherwise normal communicate if cleanup is uncertain: fixed RuntimeError(hermes_process_retirement_failed), with owner retained.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.launch_unknown: If Popen was invoked but no handle returned, source records launch_unconfirmed and retains conservative owner/path state. This is uncertainty, not proof that an OS actor was created, leaked or retired.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.usage_path: Unlink only after confirmed known process/pipe cleanup with no unresolved phase. Unconfirmed child may still write; path retention is intentional. Usage unlink is not physical erasure or a process-exit receipt.
owner_phase_and_exception_contract.old_helper: Existing _kill_process_group body stays unchanged for direct callers; _run now uses owner phase handling.

new_tests_and_overlap.causality: All use actual Popen on an inert executable, actual readiness and saved original wait/pipe operations. Strong owner checked before launch and at communicate. Fixture receipt is collected after product assertions and actual separate cleanup.

Original primary exceptions retain their existing caller traceback contract. A caller-held exception may retain frame data; the owner registry itself stores fixed phase strings, not raw errors.

Direct-child wait/known parent-pipe receipts do not establish retirement of all descendants, private SDK/native participants, allocator memory or copy destinations. Group signal is a request, not universal descendant retirement.
